title: Trying to derive an RH contraction from the decimal splice
question: does the decimal pi-over-ten phase derive eta -> c eta on the zero set of the same xi function?

verdict.conclusion: The decimal phase yields an exact golden barycentric contraction c=1/phi, and two hypothetical contracted descendants strictly reduce both the nonlinear seam defect and the central horizontal residue. But the contraction acts on a weighted coordinate or selected channel, not on the support of xi zeros. At function level the reflection average collapses to xi itself, horizontal-only contraction is nonholomorphic, and the period-20 prime twist is nonprincipal. The missing same-xi or untwisted-prime invariance is not derived.

goldenDecimalMixer.interpretation: this is an exact contraction of the barycentre or a declared output coordinate; the two input support points remain +eta and -eta

sameXiAudit.functionLevelReflectionAverage: M_p xi(s)=p xi(s)+(1-p)xi(1-s)=xi(s) by the functional equation; it does not equal xi at a contracted horizontal argument
sameXiAudit.zeroBarycentreWarning: a weighted average of two zero locations is not generally another zero
sameXiAudit.horizontalMap: T_c(eta+i gamma)=c eta+i gamma=((1+c)/2)z+((c-1)/2)conjugate(z), so it is nonholomorphic when c is not 1
sameXiAudit.holomorphicAlternative: z -> c z contracts the ordinate as well as the displacement and would create a forbidden finite accumulation if it preserved the known nonempty xi zero set under indefinite iteration

quartetStressTest.conclusion: contracting the quartet changes the entire function unless eta=0 or c^2=1

seamDefectTest.positiveSeriesBound: epsilon(c eta)<c^2 epsilon(eta) for 0<c<1 and eta nonzero in the strip

branchAndProjectionAudit.equalHalfBarycentre: (eta+(-eta))/2=0, but the branch support remains the two points +eta and -eta
branchAndProjectionAudit.goldenWeightedBarycentre: p=phi/2 and 1-p produce expectation eta/phi without moving either support point
branchAndProjectionAudit.unitaryBoundary: a lossless two-channel mixer preserves total norm and stores the missing horizontal information in the complementary output
branchAndProjectionAudit.projectionBoundary: discarding the complementary output is nonunitary postselection, not an invariance of the completed xi determinant

fourierCounterexample.input: constant vector on all 20 residue classes
fourierCounterexample.conclusion: the decimal mode can vanish while the principal mode is nonzero

finitePrimeDiagnostic.interpretation: the decimal additive twist cancels its own leading reduced-residue mean, but it is a nonprincipal residue-class channel and does not bound the untwisted Chebyshev error

conditionalTheorem.statement: If the completed decimal splice preserves the same xi zero ledger while sending every upper zero quartet to at most two descendants with displacement eta/phi, and if no zeros are born at infinity, repeated contraction forces RH.
conditionalTheorem.newGain: the factor c=1/phi is derived from the decimal phase, and two descendants still contract the exact seam defect; c is no longer an arbitrary assumed constant
missingPremises: prove that the barycentric mixer acts on zero support rather than only on an expectation or projected channel
prove same-xi closure or a globally complete no-birth genealogy
prove exact recovery of the untwisted principal von Mangoldt channel
conditionalTheorem.status: conditional RH criterion sharpened; RH remains open
